content:
rafa: Strange one. Our TypeScript sampleapp (pnpm workspace) builds fine locally but in the Edge preview the SDK default import resolves to an object where calling it throws "TypeError: createClient is not a function".

rafa: Minimal repro in repo `examples/edge-optimize-deps-weirdness`. Steps I used: 
```
git clone git@github.com:redwood-internal/edge-repros.git
cd edge-repros/examples/edge-optimize-deps-weirdness
pnpm i
# build the app and run our edge preview harness
pnpm --filter sampleapp run build
pnpm --filter sampleapp run preview:edge
```
The app imports the SDK as `import createClient from 'redwood-inference-js'` in `src/main.ts`. Works under node (dev), breaks only in edge preview.

rafa: package.json snippets:
```
// sampleapp/package.json
{ "name":"sampleapp","type":"module","dependencies":{"redwood-inference-js":"workspace:packages/sdk"} }
// sdk/package.json
{ "name":"redwood-inference-js","main":"dist/index.cjs.js","module":"dist/index.esm.js","types":"dist/index.d.ts","exports":{"import":"./dist/index.esm.js","require":"./dist/index.cjs.js"} }
```
TypeScript config has `esModuleInterop: true`. Runtime inspector in the edge preview shows the import value as `Object { __esModule: true, createClient: [Function], health: [Function] }` (i.e., named export shape) — no default function. So `import createClient from` ends up with the namespace object.

jade: Did you see any prebundling from Vite optimizeDeps? That can prebundle CJS and change shapes. Also check if the preview harness applies an additional loader transform (we run esbuild on the artifact for worker compatibility).

rafa: Yes, build output contains a small prebundle `node_modules/.vite/redwood-inference-js.js` that exports named functions. When the preview runner consumes the built artifact we run a quick esbuild pass targeting the worker which transforms `exports.createClient =` into a namespace-like object, then the app's `import default` resolves to that namespace.

frank: Hmm. So two transformations: vite prebundle (optimizeDeps) + our esbuild worker pass. The combined effect flips the module shape. Workarounds: 1) use `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-inference-js'` and then `const create = Redwood.default ?? Redwood.createClient ?? Redwood`, 2) ensure the SDK publishes an explicit `default` export in its ESM build so that the chain preserves callable default.

jade: Could also try disabling optimizeDeps for the package via `optimizeDeps.exclude` or marking the SDK as pre-built so vite doesn't prebundle it. That might keep the ESM shape through the pipeline.

rafa: I tried `optimizeDeps.exclude: ['redwood-inference-js']` and that prevented the prebundle — the final edge preview then had the expected default function in many runs. Not ideal as a long-term fix but useful as a stopgap.

frank: For the SDK: publishing an ESM entry that includes `export default createClient` in `dist/index.esm.js` would make things deterministic. Right now our ESM build only has named exports (`export function createClient...;`) so consumers who `import default` rely on bundler interop. That's fragile.

rafa: Also observed a typing fuzz: TS auto-imports created `import createClient from 'redwood-inference-js'` because `dist/index.d.ts` has `export default function createClient(...)`. But the ESM JS file has only `export function createClient`, so the types and runtime differ. That's why devs are confused.

frank: Action items: 
- SDK: add explicit default export in ESM build and ensure dist/types reflect runtime shape (RD-5010).
- Devex/sampleapp: add onboarding note about optimizeDeps and a quick vite config snippet to exclude SDK if needed.
- Preview harness: add a diagnostic that scans uploaded bundles for mismatched export shapes (presence of `__esModule` + no `default` function) and warn early (RD-5011).

ci-bot: Created ticket RD-5010: "sdk: ensure ESM build includes default export and align types".

dev-bot: Created ticket RD-5011: "preview: detect potential ESM/CJS interop issues in uploaded bundles" and linked RD-5010.

jade: Suggested vite snippet for onboarding: 
```js
// vite.config.js
export default {
  optimizeDeps: {
    exclude: ['redwood-inference-js']
  },
  build: {
    commonjsOptions: { transformMixedEsModules: true }
  }
}
```
Note: excluding the package forces Vite to preserve the import shape and avoids an extra prebundle step.

rafa: I'll add a troubleshooting section to the sampleapp README with repro steps, the optimizeDeps workaround, and the `import * as` fallback snippet. I'll post the PR link here once it's pushed.

frank: Long-term we should move SDK publishing to ESM-first with an explicit `default` export or update typings to match named-only exports and guide devs to `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference-js'`. Both are breaking in different ways so track as a release item.

rafa: TL;DR for onboarding checklist I'm adding: 1) run production edge preview early; 2) inspect bundle for prebundled vendor files (node_modules/.vite); 3) if you see interop issues, try `optimizeDeps.exclude` or use `import * as` fallback; 4) file a ticket and attach the bundle.

frank: Thanks — this should reduce "works locally" confusion. :thumbsup:
